newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTAN SCENT VICTORY AGAINST ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN SCENT VICTORY AGAINST ZIMBABWE.

text.p: Pakistan had a sight of victory against Zimbabwe after reducing the touring side's second innings to 189 for five at tea on the fifth and final day of the first test on Monday.
Zimbabwe, trailing by 178 runs on first innings, lost two more wickets in the second session before eventually wiping out the deficit. At tea they held a slender 11-run lead.
The touring team, starting the day at 38 for one, added 86 runs in the first session and another 65 runs after lunch in their battle to salvage a draw.
David Houghton was the first wicket to fall in the second session, bowled by Saqlain Mushtaq as he tried to play the off-spinner to the leg side.
Houghton's 61, his third half-century in 17 tests, contained 10 fours and came from 114 balls.
His departure at 159 was followed 18 runs later by that of Craig Wishart, who was bowled by paceman Shahid Nazir for 10.
At the interval Andy Flower was on 11 and Guy Whittall on eight.
